title: The Lesson I Learned When Jesus Slept During the Storm (Mark 4:38)
paragraphs: The Lesson I Learned When Jesus Slept During the Storm (Mark 4:38)
He was asleep.

Not absent.
Not careless.
Asleep.
That is what shook me in Mark 4:38.

The storm was screaming.
The boat was filling.
The disciples were panicking.
And Jesus was sleeping.
That used to offend me.
Because when life starts breaking apart, I do not just want Jesus in the boat. I want Him moving. I want Him explaining. I want Him fixing things before fear gets loud.
But here is the lesson the storm taught me:

Jesus sleeping was not Jesus failing.
It was Jesus revealing.

Revealing that panic does not mean He has lost control.
Revealing that waves can be violent while His throne stays steady.
Revealing that my fear says more about my trust than my situation.

The storm made the disciples think they were abandoned.
But the truth was deeper than the wind.
The Savior they were afraid of losing was already with them.
And that is where grace walks in.

Some of us are in that boat right now.
Praying.
Crying.
Wondering why heaven feels quiet.

But silence is not abandonment.
Stillness is not weakness.
And Christ resting in the storm means He is not threatened by what is threatening you.
He can sleep because He is Lord over what makes us tremble.
Then with one word, He stood up and did what no disciple could do.

He rebuked the wind.
He silenced the sea.
And He exposed the deeper storm inside their hearts.
That is my lesson:

Sometimes the greatest miracle is not that Jesus stops the storm immediately.
It is that He teaches me to trust Him while it is still raging.

And the Gospel is this: the same Jesus who calmed Galilee also went into the greater storm of sin, judgment, and death for us. At the cross, He was not sleeping. He was surrendering Himself so sinners like us could be rescued. He rose again so that every fearful heart can find peace, not in perfect circumstances, but in a perfect Savior.

So if your life feels like a sinking boat tonight, do not measure His love by the noise around you.
Measure it by the cross.
Measure it by the empty tomb.
Measure it by the fact that Jesus is still in the boat.
And if He is there, you are not abandoned.
You are being taught to trust.
